profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record is one of eleven adjacent building footprints in Compass Datacenters Red Oak development, a wholesale data center campus in Ellis County, Texas, just south of the Dallas-Fort Worth core. This particular footprint sits in the westernmost row of the campus, the southernmost of five buildings arranged along that row. Compass Datacenters own market materials describe this campus, part of its Dallas-Fort Worth market, as a 360 megawatt development that was still nearing completion as of the most recent site content reviewed, with a confirmed 200 million dollar expansion phase announced in April 2024 that added two buildings totaling more than 500,000 square feet. A separate July 2026 company news item states that Red Oak now hosts seven data centers total, though that figure appears to describe the city of Red Oak as a whole rather than Compass own building count specifically, so it should not be read as confirming exactly how many of the eleven OpenStreetMap footprints in this cluster are Compass-operated versus operated by other companies also active in the area. Compass Datacenters was founded in 2011 by Chris Crosby, a former Digital Realty senior executive who remains the company CEO, and completed its first data center, a 1.2 megawatt facility, in 2012. The company is headquartered in Dallas, Texas, and describes its current ownership, per its own about-us page, as Ontario Teachers Pension Plan, RedBird Capital Partners, and company management. Beyond Dallas-Fort Worth, Compass 2026 markets list includes active developments in Chicago Hoffman Estates, Northern Virginia Loudoun County, Toronto, and Milan, plus a newly broken-ground site in Meridian, Mississippi, alongside earlier markets including Minneapolis and Nashville that the company has since exited or transferred to independent ownership. Separately, Compass donated 12.6 million dollars to fund a 40,000 square foot workforce-training replica data center at 300 Houston School Road in Red Oak, operated by Texas State Technical College, a distinct facility from the wholesale buildings mapped here that should not be confused with them. No per-building capacity, square footage, tenant, or year-built figure could be confirmed for this specific structure within the campus, and no local government permit or tax-abatement record could be retrieved this session, so those figures are deliberately omitted rather than estimated from the campus-wide totals above.

reading.body:
This facility is one of ten buildings in Compass Datacenters' Red Oak campus in Ellis County, Texas, a wholesale development southwest of Dallas-Fort Worth that the operator has publicly described as targeting 360 megawatts at full build-out. The specific building sits in the westernmost row of the campus at the southern end. No per-building capacity has been published, so the scale of this structure relative to the full campus remains unconfirmed. A $200 million expansion announced in April 2024 added two buildings totaling more than 500,000 square feet to the campus, indicating active construction through the recent past.

The Red Oak campus does not yet have a confirmed published power figure in this registry, which is why it does not rank among Texas's 18 mapped facilities with disclosed megawatt totals despite being part of a larger development described as 360 MW. Texas has 468 megawatts of published data center capacity across 18 facilities and 133 mapped sites, meaning this campus could represent a material fraction of the state's disclosed capacity if and when a per-building or campus-wide figure is published by the operator.

This is a wholesale facility operated by Compass Datacenters, a privately held company headquartered in Dallas. The company has announced developments in multiple markets including Northern Virginia, Chicago, Toronto, and Milan, but no tenant list or specific certifications for this building have been published. Any assessment of this facility's significance to AI infrastructure depends on published capacity data that the operator has not yet disclosed for this specific structure.
